Center for Data-Driven Discovery in Biomedicine, Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19104, USA Corresponding author(s): Jo Lynne Rokita (rokita@email.chop.edu), John Maris (maris@email.chop.edu) Abstract: This protocol explains the process of how we collected MYCN, MYC, and Histone ChIP -Seq data, as well as ATAC-Seq data for neuroblastoma cell lines. This protocol is comprised of three sections: Cell Growth and Expansion for care of neuroblastoma cell lines, ChIP-Seq protocol, and ATAC-Seq Protocol. Table 1, within the document, outlines which data was collected for each cell line.

II. ChIP-Seq Protocol The ChIP-Seq Protocol is separated into four parts: Cell Fixation, Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and Library Preparation, Library Sequencing, and ChIP-Seq Analysis. Note: MYCN ChIP-Seq for Kelly and NGP was performed using a slightly varied procedure and is noted in a separate section. Freshly prepare the Formaldehyde solution (Table 3A). 2. Add 1/10th of growth media volume to the existing media in each container of cells (e.g. 1/10 volume of 20 mL of media will have 2 mL added). Gently swirl to mix, and rock the plate for 15 minutes at room temperature. 3. Stop the fixation immediately by adding 1/20th volume of the 2.5M Glycine Solution (Table 3B) to the existing media in each plate (e.g. 22 mL of growth media and Formaldehyde Solution would get 1.1 mL of Glycine Solution). Gently swirl to mix, and then allow to sit at room temperature for 5 minutes. 4. After Glycine incubation, hold the plate at a 45° angle and use a cell scraper to collect cells at the bottom edge of the plate. Use a pipette to transfer the cells to a 50 mL conical tube on ice. Keep samples on ice for the remainder of the procedure.

5. Centrifuge the tube(s) at 800 x g at 4°C for 10 minutes to pellet the cells. 6. Remove and discard the supernatant, and resuspend cells in 10 mL of chilled, sterile 1X PBS by pipetting up and down. If there are multiple tubes (e.g. from multiple plates of the same cell line), the samples can be combined at this step. 7. Centrifuge the tube again as before. Remove and discard the supernatant, then add 10 mL of chilled, sterile 1X PBS to the tube. Add 100 µL of 100 mM PMSF to the tube and pipet up and down to resuspend the cells. 8. Centrifuge the tube at 800 x g at 4°C for 10 minutes. Remove and discard the supernatant. 9. Snap-freeze cells in dry ice, and store at -80°C. 10. Ship cells to Active Motif on dry ice following the instructions listed at on the Sample Submission Form, downloaded from www.activemotif.com/sample-submission. Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and Library Preparation by Active Motif: Table 4: Antibody information and concentration used for ChIP Antibody Manufacturer, Catalog# Amount of Antibody per Immunoprecipitation (IP) Chromatin Concentration per IP N-Myc Active Motif, #61185 6 μl 30 μg c-Myc Santa Cruz N262, #sc-764 20 μl 30 μg H3K4me1 Active Motif, #39297 5 μl 30 μg H3K4me3 Active Motif, #39159 3 μl 30 μg H3K27Ac Active Motif, #39133 4 μg 30 μg HeK27me3 Millipore, #07-449 4 μg 30 μg H3K4me1 Active Motif, #39297 5 μl 30 μg Methods for chromatin immunoprecipitation and library preparation were conducted by Active Motif. In brief: 1. Chromatin was isolated using a lysis buffer and membranes were disrupted with a dounce homogenizer. 2. Lysates were sonicated with Active Motif’s EpiShear probe sonicator ( #53051) and cooled sonication platform (#53080) to an average fragment length 300-500 bp. 3. A portion of the sample was collected as the Input, treated with RNase, proteinase K, and incubated to reverse crosslinking. DNA was collected by ethanol precipitation.

4. Input DNA was resuspended and concentration was quantified by a NanoDrop spectrophotometer. Extrapolation of this concentration to the original chromatin volume allowed for quantitation of the total chromatin yield. 5. Aliquots of fixed chromatin to be used in the immunoprecipitation were precleared with protein A agarose beads (Invitrogen, #15918014). 6. Genomic DNA regions of interest were isolated using specific ChIP antibodies (Table 4). 7. Antibody DNA complexes were isolated using additional beads. 8. The crosslinked DNA, antibody, and bead complexes were washed. 9. The crosslinked DNA was eluted from the beads with an SDS buffer, and subjected to RNase and proteinase K treatment. 10. Reverse crosslinking occurred in an overnight incubation at 65°C, and ChIP DNA was purified with a phenol-chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation. 11. Illumina sequencing libraries were prepared from the ChIP and Input DNA from the ChIP and Input DNAs using the standard consecutive enzymatic steps of end-polishing, dA-addition, and adaptor ligation using Active Motif’s custom liquid handling robotics pipeline. 12. Samplers were amplified with a 15 cycle PCR amplification and then quantified before being shipped to the Jefferson Cancer Genomics Laboratory at the Kimmel Cancer Center for sequencing. Grow cells as described in Cell Growth and Expansion section of protocol to 70-80% confluence in 150 mm tissue culture plates in 20 mL of media. 2. To the existing media, add 415 µL of 37% formaldehyde (final concentration of 0.75%), and rock for 10 minutes at room temperature. 3. ChIP Library Sequencing for ChIP-Seq by Jefferson Cancer Genomics Laboratory:

Methods for sequencing were conducted by the Jefferson Cancer Genomics Laboratory at the Kimmel Cancer Center. In brief: 1. Samples were quality control tested using an Agilent High Sensitivity Screen Tape to determine average fragment length. 2. The concentration of each library was measured using a High Sensitivity Qubit Quantification kit, and samples were diluted to an appropriate amount for the loading protocol (4 nM or less). 3. Samples were normalized to the same nanomolar concentration, and libraries were pooled together in equal amounts. 4. Samples were diluted to 1.51 pM in Low EDTA TE Buffer. 5. Samples were sequenced as single-end, 70 bp reads to an average depth of ~30 M reads on a NextSeq 500. ChIP-Seq Analysis FASTQ q uality was assessed using FastQC ( http://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/)and sequences were adapter - and quality-trimmed using Trim Galore (F., 2015; Lindgreen, 2012) . Since multiple sequencers were used, FASTQ phred sequencing scores (Ewing et al., 1998) were calculated using a perl script (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/douglasgscofield/bioinfo/master/scripts/phredDetector.pl). This value was used as input into the alignment algorithm. The bwa samse (Li and Durbin, 2009) was used to align the reads to hg19 reference genome and Picard tools (Alec Wysoker, 2013) was used to remove duplicates. Fragment sizes were estimated using MaSC (Ramachandran et al., 2013) and these values were used as input into MACS2 (Zhang et al., 2008) for narrow peak calling (transcription factors) or broad peak calling (histone marks). Peaks were called significant using a q-value (minimum False Discovery Rate) cut off of 0.05. Results were returned in units of signal per million reads to get normalized peak values. Finally, repetitive centromeric, telomeric and satellite regions known to have low sequencing confidence were removed using the blacklisted regions defined by UCSC.

III. ATAC-Seq Protocol The following ATAC-Seq protocol is adapted from Buenrostro, et. al, 2015. This protocol consists of four parts: Cell Preparation, Transposition Reaction and Purification, PCR Amplification, qPCR, and Library Preparation. Primer 1 and Primer 2 were custom synthesized by Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT), using sequences provided in Buenrostro, et. al, 2015 (Table 7). Note: ATAC-Seq for NB-69 and NGP was performed using a slightly varied procedure and is noted in a separate section. To amplify Transposed DNA, combine the following into 0.2 mL PCR tube: • 10 µL transposed DNA • 10 µL nuclease-free H2O • 2.5 µL 25 µM PCR Primer 1 (Ad1) • 2.5 µL 25 µM Barcoded PCR Primer 2 (Ad2.X, X meaning the number of unique samples) • 25 µL NEBNext High-Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix

2. Thermal cycle as follows: 1 cycle: 5 min 72°C 30 sec 98°C 5 cycles: 10 sec 98°C 30 sec 63°C 1 min 72°C The five minute extension is critical to allow extension on both ends of the primer after transposition, thereby generating amplifiable fragments. This ensures that downstream quantitative PCR (qPCR) quantitation will not change the complexity of the original library. qPCR: Note: To reduce the GC and size bias in PCR, the appropriate number of PCR cycles (N) is determined using qPCR, allowing us to stop prior to saturation. 1. Keep the samples in the thermocycler following the PCR Amplification reaction and run a qPCR side reaction: • 5 µL of DNA PCR amplified DNA • 2 µL of nuclease free H2O • 1 µL of 6.25 µM Custom Nextera PCR Primer (Ad1) • 1 µL of 6.25 µM Custom Nextera PCR Primer 2 (Ad2.X) • 1 µL 9X SYBR Green I • 5 µL NEBNext High-Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix 2. Cycles on the qPCR instrument are as follows: 1 cycle: 30 sec 98°C 20 cycles: 10 sec 98°C 30 sec 63°C 1 min 72°C 3. To calculate the additional number of cycles needed, plot linear Rn versus cycle and determine the cycle number that corresponds to one-third of the maximum fluorescent intensity.

4. Run the remaining 45 µL PCR reaction to the cycle number determined by qPCR. Cycles are as follows: 1 cycle: 30 sec 98°C N cycles: 10 sec 98°C 30 sec 63°C 1 min 72°C 6. Purify the amplified library using Qiagen MinElute PCR Purification Kit. Elute purified library in 20 µL of elution buffer (Buffer EB from the MinElute Kit consisting of 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8)). Make sure that the column is dry prior to adding elution buffer to avoid ethanol contamination of final library. (Note: Sample can be stored at -20°C at this point.) 7. Purify amplified library using AMPure XP beads at a 1.8x ratio to get rid of adapter dimer, using 80% ethanol for the wash steps. Elute in 50 µL of nuclease free H2O. (Note: Sample can be parafilmed and stored at -20°C at this point, if needed.) 8. Concentration of the DNA eluted from the column should be about 30 nM. Library Preparation 1. Assess the quality of purified libraries using a Bioanalyzer High-Sensitivity DNA Analysis kit (Agilent). 2. If large, predominant peak exists around 1000 bp, remove with SPRI beads. • First, with a new vial of SPRI beads, perform size selection with various ratios to ensure large peak is removed. For example, 0.4X, 0.45X, 0.5X. Choose the ratio that removes 1000 bp fragments, but leaves 800 bp fragments. • Elute in 20 µL of nuclease-free water. Note: Samples can be parafilmed and stored at -20°C at this point. 3. Libraries were sequenced by Beijing Genomics International at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. Sequencing for ATAC-Seq by Beijing Genomics International (BGI):

Methods for sequencing were conducted by Beijing Genomics International at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. In brief: 1. Samples were quality control tested using an Agilent High Sensitivity Screen Tape to confirm average fragment sizes were ~180, 380, 580, 780, 980 bp. 2. The concentration of each library was measured using a High Sensitivity Qubit Quantification kit, to ensure they were ≥ 5.5 nM. 3. Samples were normalized and libraries were pooled together in equal amounts. 4. Samples were sequenced as paired-end, 100 bp to an average depth of 80M reads on a HiSeq 2500. ATAC-Seq for NB-69 and NGP via Active Motif: 1. Grow cells in a T-75 cm2 flask as described above. 2. Following detachment and pelleting, resuspend cells in 1.0 mL of the appropriate growth media. 3. Triturate until cells are in a homogenous single-cell suspension. 4. Using an automated cell counter, determine the volume which includes 100,000 cells. 5. Aliquot volume for 100,000 cells into a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 500 µL of sterile 1X PBS. 6. Centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C. 7. Carefully aspirate off the supernatant, and resuspend cells in 500 µL of growth media plus 5% DMSO and transfer to a 1.7 mL microfuge tube on ice. 8. Freeze the cells at a slow cooling to minimize cell lysis. A Mr. Frosty (Thermo Scientific, 5100-0001) container was used in this preparation. 11. Ship samples on dry ice to Active Motif (1914 Palomar Oaks Way, Ste 150, Carlsbad, CA 92008) following the instructions listed at on the Sample Submission Form, downloaded from www.activemotif.com/sample-submission. 12. Samples were prepared and sequenced following Active Motif’s ATAC-Seq proprietary protocol. If brief: a. Cells were thawed in a 37oC water bath, pelleted, washed with cold PBS, and tagmented as previously described (Buenrostro et al. 2013), with some modifications based on (Corces et al. 2017).

b. Cell pellets were resuspended in lysis buffer, pelleted, and tagmented using the enzyme buffer provided in the Nextera Library Prep Kit (Illumina). c. Tagmented DNA was then purified using the MinElute PCR purification kit (Qiagen), amplified with 10 cycles of PCR, and purified using Agencourt AMPure SPRI beads (Beckman Coulter). d. The resulting material was quantified using the KAPA Library Quantification Kit for Illumina platforms (KAPA Biosystems) and sequenced with PE42 sequencing on the NextSeq 500 sequencer (Illumina). ATAC-Seq Analysis Samples were quality-controlled and trimmed as described in Chip-Seq Analysis. FASTQ files were aligned using bwa aln for BGI samples (100 bp reads) and bwa mem for Active Motif samples (42 bp reads). Reads with mapping quality < 10 were discarded. Biological duplicate BAMs were merged using Picard tools. Broad peaks were called using --extsize 200 and --shift 100. Peaks were called significant using a q-value (minimum False Discovery Rate) cut off of 0.05. Results were returned in units of signal per million reads to get normalized peak values. Finally, repetitive centromeric, telomeric and satellite regions known to have low sequencing confidence were removed using the blacklisted regions defined by UCSC.
